meaning_en: To become less intense or widespread; to diminish or subside.
meaning_es: Disminuir en intensidad o extensión; ceder o remitir.
collocation: the storm abated, the pain abated
note: Often used for storms, pain, noise, or emotions easing off. Works both intransitively and transitively.

examples.en: The rain showed no sign of abating, so they decided to wait inside.
examples.es: La lluvia no daba señales de amainar, así que decidieron quedarse dentro.

examples.en: Her grief did not abate with time as much as she had hoped.
examples.es: Su dolor no remitió con el tiempo tanto como ella había esperado.

meaning_en: To regard with deep disgust or hatred.
meaning_es: Sentir una profunda aversión o repugnancia hacia algo o alguien.
note: Stronger and more visceral than 'dislike' or 'detest'; implies a gut-level revulsion.

examples.en: She abhorred any form of dishonesty, which made the revelation all the more painful.
examples.es: Aborrecía cualquier forma de deshonestidad, lo que hizo que la revelación fuera aún más dolorosa.

examples.en: He claimed to abhor violence yet showed little interest in preventing it.
examples.es: Decía aborrecer la violencia, pero mostraba escaso interés en prevenirla.

meaning_en: Harsh or irritating in manner; tending to cause friction or resentment.
meaning_es: Áspero o irritante en el trato; que tiende a generar fricción o resentimiento.
note: Borrowed from its literal sense of wearing away surfaces; used of people who rub others the wrong way.

examples.en: His abrasive management style left many staff members feeling demoralised.
examples.es: Su estilo de gestión áspero dejó a muchos empleados desmoralizados.

examples.en: She was direct, sometimes abrasive, but her feedback was always useful.
examples.es: Era directa, a veces áspera, pero su retroalimentación siempre resultaba útil.

meaning_en: Restrained in eating, drinking, or enjoyment; temperate in habit.
meaning_es: Moderado en el comer, el beber o los placeres; de hábitos sobrios.
note: Carries a slightly admiring or ironic tone depending on context; more literary than 'moderate' or 'restrained'.

examples.en: Despite the banquet spread before him, he remained abstemious as always.
examples.es: Pese al banquete que tenía delante, siguió siendo tan sobrio como siempre.

examples.en: Her abstemious habits drew curiosity from colleagues who enjoyed the office drinks cart.
examples.es: Sus hábitos sobrios despertaban la curiosidad de compañeros que sí disfrutaban del carrito de bebidas de la oficina.

meaning_en: To formally revoke or abolish a law, right, or agreement.
meaning_es: Derogar o abolir formalmente una ley, un derecho o un acuerdo.
collocation: abrogate a treaty, abrogate a law
note: A legal and political term; most common in formal contexts ('abrogate a treaty', 'abrogate a right') but also used for informal arrangements dissolved by mutual consent.

examples.en: The new administration moved swiftly to abrogate the environmental regulations.
examples.es: El nuevo gobierno actuó con rapidez para derogar la normativa medioambiental.

examples.en: Both parties agreed to abrogate the clause that had proven unenforceable.
examples.es: Ambas partes acordaron derogar la cláusula que había resultado inaplicable.

meaning_en: Difficult to understand; obscure because of complexity or specialisation.
meaning_es: Difícil de comprender; oscuro por su complejidad o especialización.
note: Most often applied to ideas, writing, or arguments; can describe a person's style when their expression is needlessly opaque.

examples.en: The lecture was so abstruse that even the graduate students struggled to follow.
examples.es: La conferencia era tan abstrusa que hasta los estudiantes de posgrado tenían dificultades para seguirla.

examples.en: He had a talent for making abstruse concepts feel accessible.
examples.es: Tenía el don de hacer accesibles los conceptos más abstrusas.

meaning_en: An expression of praise or an award recognising exceptional achievement.
meaning_es: Elogio o reconocimiento que se otorga por un logro excepcional.
note: Often used in the plural; can refer to a formal award or general high praise.

examples.en: The film collected accolades at every major festival before its wide release.
examples.es: La película acumuló reconocimientos en todos los grandes festivales antes de su estreno general.

examples.en: The highest accolade she could imagine was a positive review from that critic.
examples.es: El mayor reconocimiento que podía imaginar era una crítica positiva de ese crítico en concreto.

meaning_en: Sharply critical or biting in tone, often with a bitter edge.
meaning_es: De tono mordaz o incisivamente crítico, a menudo con cierta amargura.
note: Often describes someone's wit, tone, or criticism; suggests a cutting quality rather than merely being direct.

examples.en: Her acerbic review spared neither the director nor the cast.
examples.es: Su mordaz crítica no dejó títere con cabeza, ni entre los actores ni entre los responsables de la dirección.

examples.en: He softened his usually acerbic tone when he realised she was upset.
examples.es: Suavizó su tono habitualmente mordaz al darse cuenta de que ella estaba afectada.

meaning_en: Bitterness or ill feeling, especially in speech or manner.
meaning_es: Amargura o animosidad, especialmente en el habla o el trato.
note: The adjective form 'acrimonious' is at least as common as the noun; both describe soured relationships or debates.

examples.en: The negotiations collapsed amid acrimony after both sides accused each other of bad faith.
examples.es: Las negociaciones se rompieron entre las acusaciones mutuas de mala fe y una gran animosidad.

examples.en: The acrimony of the divorce proceedings left both parties exhausted.
examples.es: La crispación del proceso de divorcio dejó agotadas a ambas partes.

meaning_en: The ability to make quick, accurate judgements; sharpness of mind in a practical area.
meaning_es: Capacidad para emitir juicios rápidos y certeros; agudeza mental en un campo práctico.
note: Frequently modified by a domain — 'business acumen', 'political acumen' — but works fine unmodified when context is clear.

examples.en: Her financial acumen helped the company survive a period of severe market turbulence.
examples.es: Su perspicacia financiera ayudó a la empresa a superar un período de intensa turbulencia en los mercados.

examples.en: The promotion surprised no one who had witnessed his acumen in client negotiations.
examples.es: El ascenso no sorprendió a nadie que hubiera presenciado su agudeza en las negociaciones con clientes.

meaning_en: To accept or comply reluctantly but without protest.
meaning_es: Aceptar o conformarse de mala gana pero sin protestar.
collocation: acquiesce to a demand, acquiesce in a decision
note: Implies passive acceptance rather than enthusiastic agreement; often followed by 'in' or 'to'.

examples.en: Rather than prolong the argument, she acquiesced and let the matter drop.
examples.es: En lugar de prolongar la discusión, cedió y dejó correr el asunto.

examples.en: He acquiesced in the committee's decision, though he had serious reservations.
examples.es: Aceptó la decisión del comité, aunque guardaba serias reservas al respecto.

meaning_en: Refusing to be persuaded or to change one's mind.
meaning_es: Que se niega a ser convencido o a cambiar de opinión; inflexible.
note: Common predicatively ('was adamant', 'remained adamant') and before a 'that'-clause; also frequent before a noun ('adamant refusal').

examples.en: She was adamant that no exceptions would be made, regardless of the circumstances.
examples.es: Era inflexible en que no se haría ninguna excepción, independientemente de las circunstancias.

examples.en: Despite pressure from the board, the CEO remained adamant about the restructuring plan.
examples.es: A pesar de la presión del consejo, el director ejecutivo se mantuvo inflexible en su plan de reestructuración.

meaning_en: Highly skilled or proficient at something.
meaning_es: Muy hábil o competente en algo.
collocation: adept at negotiating, adept at handling
note: Followed by 'at' plus a gerund when used predicatively; attributively it precedes the noun ('an adept diplomat').

examples.en: He was adept at defusing tension before it could escalate into open conflict.
examples.es: Era hábil para neutralizar la tensión antes de que pudiera desembocar en un conflicto abierto.

examples.en: Years of practice had made her an adept carpenter who rarely consulted blueprints.
examples.es: Años de práctica la habían convertido en una carpintera consumada que rara vez necesitaba planos.

meaning_en: To warn or reprimand someone; to urge them firmly to behave better or take care.
meaning_es: Advertir o reprender a alguien; instarlo con firmeza a comportarse mejor o a ser más cuidadoso.
collocation: admonish someone for carelessness, admonish gently
note: Can range from gentle counsel to a sharp rebuke depending on context; the tone is set by the speaker, not the word itself.

examples.en: The judge admonished the witness for speaking before the question was finished.
examples.es: La jueza amonestó al testigo por hablar antes de que terminara la pregunta.

examples.en: She admonished her students to check sources before citing them in any paper.
examples.es: Amonestó a sus estudiantes para que verificaran las fuentes antes de citarlas en cualquier trabajo.

meaning_en: Clever and skilful, especially in difficult situations.
meaning_es: Hábil e ingenioso, especialmente en situaciones difíciles.
note: Can describe physical dexterity but is most often used for social or intellectual nimbleness.

examples.en: Her adroit handling of the press conference prevented the story from becoming a scandal.
examples.es: Su hábil manejo de la rueda de prensa impidió que la historia se convirtiera en un escándalo.

examples.en: He was adroit at changing the subject whenever conversations grew uncomfortable.
examples.es: Era hábil para cambiar de tema siempre que las conversaciones se tornaban incómodas.

meaning_en: Excessive admiration or flattery, often uncritical.
meaning_es: Admiración o adulación excesiva, a menudo acrítica.
note: Implies an audience's uncritical worship of a celebrity or leader; always carries a slightly critical undertone.

examples.en: The actor grew uncomfortable with the adulation that followed his breakout role.
examples.es: El actor comenzó a sentirse incómodo con la adulación que siguió a su papel de revelación.

examples.en: Constant adulation had made it difficult for her to accept honest criticism.
examples.es: La adulación constante le había dificultado aceptar las críticas sinceras.

meaning_en: Friendly, easy to talk to, and pleasant in manner.
meaning_es: Amable, accesible y agradable en el trato.
collocation: an affable host, an affable manner
note: Suggests approachability and warmth without implying deep emotional connection; slightly formal as a compliment.

examples.en: The new manager was affable with everyone, which helped ease the team's initial anxiety.
examples.es: El nuevo director era amable con todos, lo que ayudó a calmar la inquietud inicial del equipo.

examples.en: He was affable enough in person, yet his emails always felt terse and distant.
examples.es: En persona era muy afable, pero sus correos electrónicos siempre resultaban escuetos y distantes.

meaning_en: Filled with shock or horror at something unexpected or morally offensive.
meaning_es: Horrorizado o pasmado ante algo inesperado o moralmente inaceptable.
note: Most naturally predicative ('stood aghast', 'looked aghast'), though it occasionally precedes a noun in literary use.

examples.en: She looked aghast when she realised the email had been sent to the entire company.
examples.es: Se quedó horrorizada al darse cuenta de que el correo se había enviado a toda la empresa.

examples.en: He was aghast at the level of waste he discovered during the audit.
examples.es: Quedó estupefacto ante el nivel de despilfarro que descubrió durante la auditoría.

meaning_en: Brisk and eager willingness to do something.
meaning_es: Prontitud y entusiasmo al hacer algo.
collocation: with great alacrity, respond with alacrity
note: Almost always appears in the phrase 'with alacrity'; implies both speed and enthusiasm, not just speed.

examples.en: She accepted the invitation with alacrity, delighted to attend the opening night.
examples.es: Aceptó la invitación con prontitud y entusiasmo, encantada de asistir al estreno.

examples.en: The volunteers responded with alacrity when the shelter put out a call for help.
examples.es: Los voluntarios respondieron de inmediato cuando el refugio pidió ayuda.

meaning_en: To diminish or put to rest fears, concerns, pain, or other distressing feelings.
meaning_es: Aliviar o disipar temores, preocupaciones, dolor u otras sensaciones angustiosas.
collocation: allay fears, allay concerns, allay pain
note: Most common with 'fears', 'concerns', and 'anxieties', but also used with 'pain', 'grief', or 'hunger' in both literal and figurative senses.

examples.en: The minister held a briefing to allay public fears about the new policy.
examples.es: La ministra ofreció una rueda de prensa para disipar los temores de la opinión pública sobre la nueva política.

examples.en: Nothing she said could allay his suspicions that something had gone wrong.
examples.es: Nada de lo que ella dijo logró disipar sus sospechas de que algo había salido mal.

meaning_en: Cool and distant in manner; not friendly or forthcoming.
meaning_es: Frío y distante en el trato; que no muestra calidez ni apertura.
note: Can describe a deliberate stance ('stand aloof from politics') or simply a social manner; not inherently negative.

examples.en: Colleagues found him aloof at first, though he warmed up once he trusted people.
examples.es: Al principio, sus compañeros lo veían distante, aunque se abría una vez que confiaba en las personas.

examples.en: She stayed aloof from the gossip that swirled around the department.
examples.es: Se mantuvo al margen de los cotilleos que circulaban por el departamento.

meaning_en: Showing an unselfish concern for the welfare of others.
meaning_es: Que muestra una preocupación desinteresada por el bienestar de los demás.
note: Often questioned or qualified in everyday speech ('is it truly altruistic?'); the concept invites scepticism.

examples.en: His decision to donate anonymously seemed genuinely altruistic rather than motivated by reputation.
examples.es: Su decisión de donar de forma anónima parecía genuinamente altruista, no motivada por la reputación.

examples.en: Critics argued that the company's charitable work was anything but altruistic.
examples.es: Los críticos sostenían que la labor benéfica de la empresa no tenía nada de altruista.

meaning_en: Having mixed or contradictory feelings about something at the same time.
meaning_es: Que tiene sentimientos contradictorios o mezclados sobre algo al mismo tiempo.
collocation: ambivalent about the decision, feel ambivalent
note: Describes a genuine internal conflict, not mere indifference; followed by 'about' plus a noun or gerund.

examples.en: She was ambivalent about the promotion — excited by the opportunity but wary of the extra pressure.
examples.es: Le generaba sentimientos encontrados el ascenso: la oportunidad la entusiasmaba, pero la presión adicional le daba respeto.

examples.en: The film received an ambivalent response — praised for its ambition yet criticised for its length.
examples.es: La película tuvo una acogida ambivalente: se elogió su ambición, pero se criticó su duración.

meaning_en: To make something bad or unsatisfactory better.
meaning_es: Mejorar algo malo o insatisfactorio; paliar una situación negativa.
note: Slightly more formal than 'improve'; implies starting from a bad baseline and moving toward acceptable.

examples.en: The aid package was designed to ameliorate the worst effects of the drought.
examples.es: El paquete de ayuda estaba diseñado para paliar los peores efectos de la sequía.

examples.en: Small changes to the schedule did little to ameliorate the staff's sense of overwork.
examples.es: Los pequeños cambios en el horario hicieron poco por aliviar la sensación de sobrecarga del personal.

meaning_en: Unlikely to cause offence or controversy because it is bland or vague.
meaning_es: Que difícilmente ofende o genera controversia por ser insulso o vago.
note: The medical sense (pain-relieving) is largely obsolete; today it almost always carries mild criticism.

examples.en: The committee's anodyne statement satisfied nobody but offended no one either.
examples.es: El comunicado anodino del comité no satisfizo a nadie, pero tampoco ofendió a nadie.

examples.en: He gave an anodyne answer that revealed nothing and committed him to nothing.
examples.es: Dio una respuesta anodina que no revelaba nada ni lo comprometía con nada.

meaning_en: Apt or appropriate in the circumstances; relevantly placed.
meaning_es: Adecuado o apropiado a las circunstancias; pertinente.
note: More specific than 'relevant'; implies a pleasing, well-chosen fit between remark and moment.

examples.en: The speaker chose an apposite quotation that captured the mood of the audience perfectly.
examples.es: La oradora eligió una cita muy pertinente que captó perfectamente el estado de ánimo del público.

examples.en: His analogy was apposite: everyone in the room immediately grasped the argument.
examples.es: Su analogía era muy acertada: todos los presentes captaron el argumento de inmediato.

meaning_en: To pacify or placate someone by acceding to their demands.
meaning_es: Aplacar o apaciguar a alguien cediendo a sus exigencias.
note: Often carries a slightly negative connotation — suggesting the concession is unwise or cowardly.

examples.en: The concession was meant to appease protesters, but it only emboldened them to demand more.
examples.es: La concesión pretendía apaciguar a los manifestantes, pero solo los animó a exigir más.

examples.en: She grew tired of trying to appease a colleague who was never satisfied.
examples.es: Se cansó de intentar aplacar a una compañera que nunca quedaba satisfecha.

meaning_en: Very enthusiastic or passionate about something.
meaning_es: Muy entusiasta o apasionado por algo.
note: Slightly elevated but not rare; works for beliefs, causes, and people. Does not require romantic context.

examples.en: She was an ardent supporter of electoral reform long before it became fashionable.
examples.es: Era una ferviente defensora de la reforma electoral mucho antes de que se pusiera de moda.

examples.en: His ardent belief in the project kept the team going through months of setbacks.
examples.es: Su ferviente fe en el proyecto mantuvo al equipo en marcha durante meses de contratiempos.

meaning_en: Demanding great effort or endurance; very difficult or tiring.
meaning_es: Que exige gran esfuerzo o resistencia; muy difícil o agotador.
note: Implies sustained physical or mental effort; 'hard' or 'tough' are informal equivalents.

examples.en: The ascent was arduous, but the view from the summit made every step worthwhile.
examples.es: El ascenso era agotador, pero la vista desde la cima hacía que cada paso mereciera la pena.

examples.en: Rebuilding trust after a betrayal is an arduous process with no guaranteed outcome.
examples.es: Reconstruir la confianza tras una traición es un proceso arduo sin resultado garantizado.

meaning_en: Characterised by severe self-discipline and the avoidance of all forms of indulgence.
meaning_es: Caracterizado por una severa autodisciplina y la renuncia a todo tipo de indulgencia.
note: Has roots in religious tradition but is now used more broadly for anyone with markedly spare, self-denying habits.

examples.en: The philosopher lived an ascetic life, owning little and spending nothing on luxury.
examples.es: El filósofo llevaba una vida ascética: poseía pocas cosas y no gastaba nada en lujos.

examples.en: Her ascetic approach to training set her apart from teammates who enjoyed their rest days.
examples.es: Su enfoque ascético del entrenamiento la distinguía de sus compañeras, que sí disfrutaban de los días de descanso.

meaning_en: Showing great care, persistence, and hard work.
meaning_es: Que muestra gran esmero, perseverancia y dedicación al trabajo.
note: Emphasises consistent, careful effort over time rather than a single burst of energy.

examples.en: Her assiduous note-taking made her the most prepared student in the seminar.
examples.es: Su meticulosa toma de apuntes la convirtió en la estudiante más preparada del seminario.

examples.en: He was assiduous in answering every reader's question, no matter how trivial.
examples.es: Respondía con esmero cada pregunta de los lectores, por trivial que fuera.

meaning_en: Able to accurately assess situations and turn them to one's advantage; shrewd.
meaning_es: Capaz de evaluar situaciones con precisión y sacar ventaja de ellas; perspicaz.
note: Positive term implying both intelligence and practical savvy; 'astute businessman' is a common collocation.

examples.en: She made an astute observation about the market that her rivals had completely missed.
examples.es: Hizo una observación perspicaz sobre el mercado que sus rivales habían pasado completamente por alto.

examples.en: His astute reading of the political climate helped him avoid several potential blunders.
examples.es: Su perspicaz lectura del clima político le ayudó a evitar varios errores potenciales.

meaning_en: Severe in appearance or manner; lacking comfort, decoration, or warmth.
meaning_es: Severo en apariencia o en trato; carente de comodidad, adorno o calidez.
note: Used of people, places, and policies; 'austerity' in economics extends this to government spending cuts.

examples.en: The courtroom was spare and austere, designed to project authority rather than comfort.
examples.es: La sala era sobria y austera, diseñada para proyectar autoridad más que comodidad.

examples.en: He was raised in austere conditions that gave him an instinctive dislike of waste.
examples.es: Creció en condiciones de austeridad que le inculcaron un rechazo instintivo al despilfarro.

meaning_en: Strongly disinclined or opposed to something.
meaning_es: Que siente una fuerte aversión u oposición hacia algo.
collocation: averse to risk, averse to change
note: Typically predicative and followed by 'to'; 'risk-averse' shows it also forms compounds used attributively.

examples.en: She was averse to confrontation, which sometimes made difficult conversations harder to have.
examples.es: Era reacia a la confrontación, lo que a veces dificultaba aún más las conversaciones difíciles.

examples.en: The organisation was deeply averse to change, even when change was clearly needed.
examples.es: La organización era profundamente reacia al cambio, incluso cuando este era claramente necesario.

meaning_en: Having or showing a keen interest in or enthusiasm for something.
meaning_es: Que muestra un gran interés o entusiasmo por algo.
note: Usually attributive ('avid fan', 'avid reader'); implies regular, enthusiastic engagement rather than a single encounter.

examples.en: She was an avid reader who finished at least three books a week.
examples.es: Era una lectora voraz que terminaba al menos tres libros por semana.

examples.en: His avid interest in local history led him to spend every weekend in archives.
examples.es: Su apasionado interés por la historia local lo llevaba a pasar todos los fines de semana en archivos.

meaning_en: Lacking originality or freshness; drearily commonplace.
meaning_es: Carente de originalidad o frescura; tristemente vulgar o trivial.
note: The noun 'banality' is equally common; 'the banality of evil' (Arendt) is a well-known phrase that extended the word's cultural reach.

examples.en: The speech was competent but banal, containing nothing the audience hadn't heard before.
examples.es: El discurso era competente pero banal, y no contenía nada que el público no hubiera oído antes.

examples.en: He found small talk banal and struggled at the kind of parties where it was expected.
examples.es: Encontraba la conversación trivial aburrida y le costaba en el tipo de reuniones donde se esperaba.

meaning_en: Owing thanks or having a duty to someone because of their help or favour.
meaning_es: Que debe gratitud o tiene una obligación con alguien por su ayuda o favor.
collocation: beholden to no one, feel beholden
note: Always predicative; often negated ('beholden to no one') to assert independence from obligation.

examples.en: She accepted no funding from industry groups so she could remain beholden to no one.
examples.es: No aceptaba financiación de grupos industriales para no quedar en deuda con nadie.

examples.en: He felt beholden to the mentor who had given him his first real break in the field.
examples.es: Se sentía en deuda con el mentor que le había dado su primera gran oportunidad en el sector.

meaning_en: Aggressively warlike or hostile in manner.
meaning_es: De carácter agresivamente belicoso u hostil.
note: Used of nations, leaders, and rhetoric; not typically applied to physical altercations between private individuals.

examples.en: The bellicose speeches from both sides made a diplomatic resolution seem increasingly unlikely.
examples.es: Los discursos belicosos de ambas partes hacían que una resolución diplomática pareciera cada vez menos probable.

examples.en: His bellicose manner in meetings made colleagues reluctant to challenge him directly.
examples.es: Su actitud belicosa en las reuniones hacía que los compañeros se resistieran a cuestionarle directamente.

meaning_en: Gentle and kindly in nature; not causing harm.
meaning_es: De naturaleza apacible y bondadosa; que no causa daño.
note: Also used in medicine for non-cancerous tumours; the general sense always implies harmlessness and mild goodwill.

examples.en: The regulation had the benign aim of protecting small businesses from price manipulation.
examples.es: La regulación tenía el benévolo objetivo de proteger a las pequeñas empresas de la manipulación de precios.

examples.en: Her expression was benign but gave nothing away about what she was actually thinking.
examples.es: Su expresión era apacible, pero no revelaba nada sobre lo que realmente estaba pensando.

meaning_en: Cheerfully carefree; showing a casual lack of concern.
meaning_es: Despreocupado y alegre; que muestra una indiferencia casual.
note: Can mean pleasantly carefree (literary) or irresponsibly untroubled (modern critical use); context clarifies.

examples.en: She proceeded with blithe disregard for the consequences of what she was about to say.
examples.es: Continuó con despreocupada indiferencia hacia las consecuencias de lo que estaba a punto de decir.

examples.en: His blithe assumption that everything would work out was either admirable or reckless.
examples.es: Su despreocupada convicción de que todo saldría bien era o bien admirable o bien temeraria.

meaning_en: Rough, bad-mannered, and unpleasant in social situations.
meaning_es: Grosero, maleducado y desagradable en situaciones sociales.
note: 'Boor' (the noun) is less common; the adjective is the more typical form in modern use.

examples.en: His boorish behaviour at the dinner table made the rest of the guests visibly uncomfortable.
examples.es: Su comportamiento grosero en la mesa hizo que el resto de los invitados se sintieran claramente incómodos.

examples.en: She quietly walked away from the boorish comment rather than dignify it with a response.
examples.es: Se alejó en silencio del comentario maleducado en lugar de dignificarlo con una respuesta.

meaning_en: Bold and shameless in a way that ignores expected social norms.
meaning_es: Descarado y desvergonzado de un modo que ignora las normas sociales esperadas.
note: Negative connotation; the boldness is considered offensive, not admirable. 'Brazen it out' means to face shame without flinching.

examples.en: The officials issued a brazen denial despite overwhelming evidence to the contrary.
examples.es: Los funcionarios emitieron un descarado desmentido pese a las abrumadoras pruebas en contrario.

examples.en: She decided to brazen it out rather than offer any explanation for her absence.
examples.es: Decidió hacerse la desentendida en lugar de dar cualquier explicación por su ausencia.

meaning_en: Abrupt or offhand in speech or manner.
meaning_es: Brusco o cortante en el habla o en el trato.
note: Implies curtness without necessarily meaning to be rude; can be a personality trait rather than a deliberate slight.

examples.en: Her brusque reply left him unsure whether she was annoyed or simply busy.
examples.es: Su respuesta brusca le dejó sin saber si estaba irritada o simplemente ocupada.

examples.en: He was famously brusque with reporters but charming at small dinner parties.
examples.es: Era notoriamente brusco con los periodistas, pero encantador en pequeñas cenas privadas.

meaning_en: To persuade someone to do something by flattery or gentle repeated pressure.
meaning_es: Persuadir a alguien para que haga algo mediante halagos o una suave insistencia.
note: Implies gentle manipulation; the object is usually a person and the construction is 'cajole someone into'.

examples.en: She cajoled her reluctant colleague into joining the cross-departmental committee.
examples.es: Convenció con halagos a su reticente compañero para que se uniera al comité interdepartamental.

examples.en: He spent an hour trying to cajole the stubborn printer into producing a single clean copy.
examples.es: Pasó una hora intentando convencer a la terca impresora de que produjera una sola copia limpia.

meaning_en: Showing an insensitive and cruel disregard for others' feelings.
meaning_es: Que muestra una insensible y cruel indiferencia ante los sentimientos ajenos.
note: Stronger and more morally charged than 'insensitive'; can describe someone who has hardened over time as well as someone acting with cold intent.

examples.en: The landlord's callous response to the family's eviction shocked even local officials.
examples.es: La respuesta despiadada del propietario ante el desahucio de la familia sorprendió incluso a los funcionarios locales.

examples.en: She was callous about the redundancies, citing numbers without acknowledging the human cost.
examples.es: Fue insensible respecto a los despidos: citó cifras sin reconocer el coste humano.

meaning_en: Truthful and straightforward, even when the truth is uncomfortable.
meaning_es: Sincero y directo, incluso cuando la verdad resulta incómoda.
note: 'Candid' implies voluntary openness; 'frank' is a close synonym. A candid photo is one taken naturally, not posed.

examples.en: I want your candid opinion — not what you think I want to hear.
examples.es: Quiero tu opinión sincera, no lo que crees que quiero escuchar.

examples.en: The CEO gave a surprisingly candid interview about the years the company nearly failed.
examples.es: El director ejecutivo concedió una entrevista sorprendentemente sincera sobre los años en que la empresa estuvo a punto de quebrar.

meaning_en: Given to sudden unpredictable changes in mood, behaviour, or opinion.
meaning_es: Que cambia de humor, comportamiento u opinión de forma repentina e impredecible.
note: Can describe people, institutions, weather, or abstract forces ('capricious markets'); always implies unpredictability.

examples.en: Working for such a capricious boss made long-term planning almost impossible.
examples.es: Trabajar para un jefe tan caprichoso hacía que la planificación a largo plazo fuera casi imposible.

examples.en: The weather on the coast was capricious — brilliant sunshine one moment, rain the next.
examples.es: El tiempo en la costa era caprichoso: sol brillante en un momento y lluvia al siguiente.

meaning_en: Showing a lack of proper concern or respect; dismissively offhand.
meaning_es: Que muestra una falta de consideración o respeto; desdeñosamente displicente.
note: Always negative in modern use; the historical 'cavalier' as a nobleman or royalist is unrelated to this sense.

examples.en: His cavalier attitude toward deadlines frustrated every team he worked with.
examples.es: Su actitud displicente hacia los plazos frustraba a todos los equipos con los que trabajaba.

examples.en: She was cavalier about data security in a way that made the IT department uneasy.
examples.es: Era descuidada con la seguridad de los datos de un modo que inquietaba al departamento de informática.

meaning_en: To express strong official disapproval of someone or their actions.
meaning_es: Expresar una fuerte desaprobación oficial hacia alguien o sus actos.
collocation: censure a politician, vote of censure
note: Refers to formal official disapproval, such as from a parliament or professional body; stronger than mere criticism.

examples.en: The committee voted to censure the member for his conduct during the hearing.
examples.es: El comité votó para censurar al miembro por su conducta durante la audiencia.

examples.en: International bodies censured the government for its handling of the refugee crisis.
examples.es: Los organismos internacionales censuraron al gobierno por su gestión de la crisis de refugiados.

meaning_en: Distress or embarrassment caused by failure or humiliation.
meaning_es: Disgusto o vergüenza causados por un fracaso o una humillación.
collocation: to his chagrin, much to her chagrin
note: Almost always appears in the phrase 'to someone's chagrin'; refers to embarrassed disappointment, not rage.

examples.en: To her great chagrin, the autocorrect had changed her boss's name throughout the report.
examples.es: Para su gran bochorno, el corrector automático había cambiado el nombre de su jefe a lo largo de todo el informe.

examples.en: Much to his chagrin, the flight he had booked landed at the wrong airport.
examples.es: Para su contrariedad, el vuelo que había reservado aterrizó en el aeropuerto equivocado.

meaning_en: Wary and unwilling to take risks; careful to consider all circumstances.
meaning_es: Cauto y poco dispuesto a correr riesgos; cuidadoso en considerar todas las circunstancias.
collocation: circumspect about plans, a circumspect approach
note: Closer to 'cautious' than 'suspicious'; implies prudent judgment rather than timidity.

examples.en: The lawyer advised her to be circumspect when discussing the case with anyone outside the firm.
examples.es: El abogado le aconsejó que fuera cautelosa al hablar del caso con personas ajenas al bufete.

examples.en: He was circumspect about making promises he might not be able to keep.
examples.es: Era prudente a la hora de hacer promesas que quizá no pudiera cumplir.

meaning_en: Mercy or leniency shown, especially towards an offender or enemy.
meaning_es: Clemencia o indulgencia que se muestra, especialmente hacia un delincuente o enemigo.
note: Typically used in legal or political contexts; the related adjective is 'clement'.

examples.en: The family appealed for clemency, arguing that the sentence was disproportionate to the offence.
examples.es: La familia apeló a la clemencia, argumentando que la pena era desproporcionada respecto al delito.

examples.en: The governor was not known for clemency and had never commuted a death sentence.
examples.es: El gobernador no era conocido por su clemencia y nunca había conmutado una pena de muerte.

meaning_en: To persuade someone to do something by force or threats.
meaning_es: Obligar a alguien a hacer algo mediante la fuerza o amenazas.
note: Implies that genuine consent is absent; often used in legal contexts to challenge agreements or statements.

examples.en: He said he had been coerced into signing the document under threat of dismissal.
examples.es: Dijo que lo habían obligado a firmar el documento bajo amenaza de despido.

examples.en: The organisation was accused of coercing donors into giving more than they could afford.
examples.es: Se acusó a la organización de coaccionar a los donantes para que dieran más de lo que podían permitirse.

meaning_en: Powerfully and persuasively expressed; convincing.
meaning_es: Expresado de manera poderosa y persuasiva; convincente.
note: Almost always applied to arguments, reasoning, or explanations; emphasises clarity and logical force together.

examples.en: She made a cogent case for restructuring the department that the board found difficult to ignore.
examples.es: Presentó argumentos convincentes a favor de la reestructuración del departamento que la junta no pudo ignorar.

examples.en: The report was cogent and well-sourced, leaving little room for the committee to object.
examples.es: El informe era convincente y estaba bien documentado, lo que dejaba poco margen para que el comité se opusiera.

meaning_en: Smugly satisfied with oneself or one's situation, to a degree that invites problems.
meaning_es: Satisfecho de sí mismo o de su situación de forma que puede generar problemas.
note: Warns of the danger of unwarranted self-satisfaction; 'complacency' is the more common nominal form.

examples.en: The team grew complacent after their early lead and nearly threw away the advantage.
examples.es: El equipo se volvió confiado tras su ventaja inicial y casi desperdició la delantera.

examples.en: Success can breed complacency in organisations that stop questioning what made them effective.
examples.es: El éxito puede engendrar complacencia en las organizaciones que dejan de cuestionar lo que las hacía eficaces.

meaning_en: A feeling of anxiety or dismay, typically caused by something unexpected.
meaning_es: Sentimiento de angustia o estupor, generalmente provocado por algo inesperado.
note: Implies stunned disbelief as much as anxiety; usually triggered by an unexpected announcement or discovery.

examples.en: The sudden cancellation caused consternation among the thousands of ticket holders.
examples.es: La cancelación repentina causó consternación entre los miles de poseedores de entradas.

examples.en: To general consternation, the keynote speaker announced that the conference would not continue.
examples.es: Para consternación general, el conferenciante principal anunció que el congreso no seguiría adelante.

meaning_en: Causing or likely to cause argument or controversy.
meaning_es: Que causa o es susceptible de causar discusión o controversia.
note: Can also describe a person who is argumentative by nature, though this is less common.

examples.en: The redistricting plan was contentious and dominated local politics for two years.
examples.es: El plan de redistribución electoral fue controvertido y dominó la política local durante dos años.

examples.en: She wisely avoided the most contentious subjects at the family reunion.
examples.es: Sabiamente evitó los temas más controvertidos en la reunión familiar.

meaning_en: Feeling or expressing remorse for one's wrongdoing.
meaning_es: Que siente o expresa arrepentimiento por sus malas acciones.
note: Implies genuine remorse, not a performance; sounding contrite but not being so is a common ironic usage.

examples.en: He appeared contrite at the hearing, but his subsequent behaviour told a different story.
examples.es: Pareció arrepentido en la audiencia, pero su comportamiento posterior contó una historia diferente.

examples.en: She wrote a contrite letter to the client, acknowledging every error her team had made.
examples.es: Escribió una carta de disculpa al cliente en la que reconocía todos los errores que había cometido su equipo.

meaning_en: Excessively complex and difficult to follow; unnecessarily complicated.
meaning_es: Excesivamente complejo y difícil de seguir; innecesariamente complicado.
note: Implies complexity that could be avoided; unlike 'intricate', which can be neutral or admiring.

examples.en: The contract was so convoluted that even the lawyers had trouble explaining what it meant.
examples.es: El contrato era tan enrevesado que incluso los abogados tenían dificultades para explicar su significado.

examples.en: His directions were convoluted and led her straight to the wrong side of the city.
examples.es: Sus indicaciones eran tan confusas que la llevaron directamente al extremo equivocado de la ciudad.

meaning_en: Abundant in supply; existing in large amounts.
meaning_es: Que existe en gran cantidad; abundante.
note: Most naturally collocates with 'notes', 'amounts', 'tears', or 'evidence'; 'copious amounts of' is nearly idiomatic.

examples.en: She took copious notes during the lecture, determined not to miss a single point.
examples.es: Tomó copiosos apuntes durante la conferencia, decidida a no perder ni un solo punto.

examples.en: The project required copious amounts of both data and patience to complete.
examples.es: El proyecto requería grandes cantidades tanto de datos como de paciencia para completarse.

meaning_en: To confirm or give support to a statement, theory, or finding.
meaning_es: Confirmar o reforzar una afirmación, teoría o hallazgo.
note: Specifically implies independent evidence supporting something; common in legal, scientific, and journalistic contexts.

examples.en: A second witness came forward to corroborate the original account of events.
examples.es: Un segundo testigo se presentó para corroborar la versión original de los hechos.

examples.en: The new data corroborated the findings from the earlier study, which strengthened the case.
examples.es: Los nuevos datos corroboraron los resultados del estudio anterior, lo que reforzó la argumentación.

meaning_en: Contemptibly lacking in courage; abjectly cowardly.
meaning_es: Que carece de valor de manera despreciable; cobarde en extremo.
note: A strong insult; implies not just fear but a shameful failure to act despite a clear obligation to do so.

examples.en: Commentators labelled the government's failure to act on the report craven and inexcusable.
examples.es: Los comentaristas calificaron de cobarde e inexcusable la inacción del gobierno ante el informe.

examples.en: Abandoning his colleague at the first sign of trouble was, by any measure, a craven act.
examples.es: Abandonar a su compañero al primer indicio de problemas fue, en cualquier medida, un acto cobarde.

meaning_en: Responsible for a fault or wrong; deserving blame.
meaning_es: Responsable de una falta o error; que merece ser culpado.
note: Legal-leaning but also used generally; 'culpable negligence' and 'culpable homicide' are established legal phrases.

examples.en: The inquiry found the contractor culpable for the structural failures that led to the collapse.
examples.es: La investigación consideró al contratista culpable de los fallos estructurales que condujeron al derrumbe.

examples.en: Several senior officials were found culpable for the misuse of public funds.
examples.es: Varios altos funcionarios fueron hallados culpables del uso indebido de fondos públicos.

meaning_en: Hasty and not thorough; superficially done.
meaning_es: Apresurado y poco detallado; hecho de manera superficial.
note: Implies that more care should have been taken; 'a cursory reading' suggests the speaker barely engaged with the material.

examples.en: Even a cursory glance at the accounts revealed that something was seriously wrong.
examples.es: Incluso un vistazo superficial a las cuentas revelaba que algo andaba muy mal.

examples.en: He gave the proposal a cursory read and approved it without asking a single question.
examples.es: Le dio una lectura superficial a la propuesta y la aprobó sin hacer ni una sola pregunta.

meaning_en: To make someone feel intimidated or discouraged.
meaning_es: Intimidar o desalentar a alguien.
note: More commonly encountered as 'daunting' (adj.) than as a finite verb; 'nothing daunted' is an established idiomatic phrase.

examples.en: The scale of the renovation was daunting, but they decided to press on regardless.
examples.es: La magnitud de la renovación era intimidante, pero decidieron seguir adelante de todos modos.

examples.en: She refused to be daunted by the hostile reception her paper received at the conference.
examples.es: Se negó a dejarse intimidar por la recepción hostil que tuvo su ponencia en el congreso.

meaning_en: A scarcity or lack of something.
meaning_es: Escasez o carencia de algo.
collocation: a dearth of evidence, a dearth of talent
note: Most naturally collocates as 'a dearth of'; the shortage implied is typically notable or problematic rather than minor.

examples.en: There was a dearth of affordable housing in the city, which worsened every year.
examples.es: Había una grave escasez de vivienda asequible en la ciudad, que empeoraba año tras año.

examples.en: The report highlighted a dearth of female voices in senior editorial positions.
examples.es: El informe señalaba la escasez de voces femeninas en los puestos editoriales de mayor rango.

meaning_en: Confident, charming, and stylish in a relaxed, effortless way.
meaning_es: Seguro, encantador y elegante de una manera relajada y aparentemente sin esfuerzo.
note: Carries an old-fashioned, slightly cinematic air; often applied to men but not exclusively so.

examples.en: He arrived late but debonair, making even his tardiness seem like part of the plan.
examples.es: Llegó tarde pero con una soltura encantadora, haciendo que incluso su retraso pareciera parte del plan.

examples.en: There was something debonair about the way she fielded the difficult questions without breaking stride.
examples.es: Había algo de donaire en la manera en que respondía a las preguntas difíciles sin perder la compostura.

meaning_en: To publicly condemn or denounce something as wrong or bad.
meaning_es: Condenar o denunciar públicamente algo como erróneo o perjudicial.
note: Slightly stronger and more formal than 'criticise'; directed at actions, policies, or conditions, though individuals can also be decried for specific behaviour.

examples.en: Artists and educators joined together to decry the funding cuts to public schools.
examples.es: Artistas y educadores se unieron para denunciar los recortes en la financiación de las escuelas públicas.

examples.en: She was quick to decry the decision but offered no concrete alternative.
examples.es: Se apresuró a condenar la decisión, pero no ofreció ninguna alternativa concreta.

meaning_en: Showing great respect and deference to another person's authority or judgement.
meaning_es: Que muestra gran respeto y deferencia hacia la autoridad o el juicio de otra persona.
note: Can imply appropriate respect or, depending on context, an excess of submission.

examples.en: Journalists were notably deferential toward the minister at the early press conference.
examples.es: Los periodistas mostraron una deferencia notable hacia la ministra en la primera rueda de prensa.

examples.en: She was deferential to the senior partner without being obsequious.
examples.es: Mostraba deferencia hacia el socio principal sin llegar a ser servil.

meaning_en: Causing harm or damage.
meaning_es: Que causa daño o perjuicio.
note: A formal, scientific-register alternative to 'harmful'; often precedes 'effects' or 'impact'.

examples.en: The study confirmed the deleterious effects of prolonged exposure to particulate pollution.
examples.es: El estudio confirmó los efectos perjudiciales de la exposición prolongada a la contaminación por partículas.

examples.en: Constant interruptions had a deleterious impact on her ability to do deep, focused work.
examples.es: Las interrupciones constantes tenían un impacto perjudicial en su capacidad para realizar un trabajo profundo y concentrado.

meaning_en: To raise objections or show reluctance.
meaning_es: Poner objeciones o mostrar renuencia.
collocation: without demur, demur at a suggestion
note: 'Without demur' means without objection. As a noun, 'demur' appears in the phrase 'without demur'.

examples.en: She accepted the additional responsibilities without demur, though she was already overstretched.
examples.es: Aceptó las responsabilidades adicionales sin rechistar, aunque ya estaba sobrecargada.

examples.en: He demurred when asked to sign off on a report he had not had time to review.
examples.es: Puso reparos cuando le pidieron que firmara un informe que no había tenido tiempo de revisar.

meaning_en: Expressing contempt or ridicule.
meaning_es: Que expresa desprecio o burla.
note: Stronger than 'mocking'; implies a certain contempt for the target, not merely amusement at their expense.

examples.en: His proposal was met with derisive laughter from the back of the room.
examples.es: Su propuesta fue acogida con risas burlonas desde el fondo de la sala.

examples.en: She brushed off the derisive comments and continued presenting her findings.
examples.es: Ignoró los comentarios despectivos y continuó presentando sus conclusiones.

meaning_en: Lacking a clear plan or purpose; going from one thing to another without enthusiasm.
meaning_es: Que carece de un plan o propósito claros; que pasa de una cosa a otra sin entusiasmo.
note: Implies that the activity is barely half-hearted; 'desultory' efforts or reading suggest drift rather than engagement.

examples.en: The negotiations dragged on with desultory progress and no clear end in sight.
examples.es: Las negociaciones avanzaban con lentitud y sin rumbo claro, sin visos de llegar a un acuerdo.

examples.en: He made a desultory attempt at tidying the office before giving up and going home.
examples.es: Hizo un intento sin convicción de ordenar la oficina antes de rendirse y marcharse a casa.

meaning_en: Modest or shy because of a lack of self-confidence.
meaning_es: Modesto o tímido por falta de confianza en uno mismo.
collocation: a diffident manner, diffident about one's achievements
note: Implies a reluctance to put oneself forward; differs from 'shy' in being more specifically about self-doubt.

examples.en: Despite his expertise, he was diffident in large groups and rarely spoke up.
examples.es: A pesar de su experiencia, era apocado en grupos grandes y rara vez tomaba la palabra.

examples.en: She was diffident about calling herself a writer, even after three published novels.
examples.es: Era reticente a llamarse escritora, incluso después de tres novelas publicadas.

meaning_en: A person who takes up a subject out of casual interest without serious study.
meaning_es: Persona que se acerca a una materia por interés casual y sin un estudio serio.
collocation: a mere dilettante, dismiss someone as a dilettante
note: Often a mild insult implying someone lacks the depth or rigour of a specialist; can also be used self-deprecatingly.

examples.en: Critics dismissed him as a dilettante who lacked the rigour of a professional historian.
examples.es: Los críticos lo descartaban como un aficionado que carecía del rigor de un historiador profesional.

examples.en: She was tired of being treated as a dilettante simply because she worked across disciplines.
examples.es: Estaba cansada de que la trataran como una aficionada simplemente porque trabajaba en varias disciplinas.

meaning_en: Not candid or sincere, typically by pretending not to know something one knows.
meaning_es: Que no es sincero o franco, generalmente fingiendo ignorar algo que sabe.
note: More diplomatic than 'dishonest'; often used to call out misleading statements without direct accusation of lying.

examples.en: It would be disingenuous to claim we were unaware of the risks at that point.
examples.es: Sería poco honesto afirmar que desconocíamos los riesgos en ese momento.

examples.en: His concern seemed disingenuous given that he had voted against the measure twice.
examples.es: Su preocupación parecía fingida dado que había votado en contra de la medida en dos ocasiones.

meaning_en: Markedly different in kind or nature; made up of elements that have little in common.
meaning_es: Marcadamente diferente en naturaleza; que consta de elementos que tienen poco en común.
note: Implies more than mere variety — the elements feel like they belong to different categories; 'disparate views', 'disparate communities'.

examples.en: The survey drew together disparate communities that had previously had little reason to interact.
examples.es: La encuesta reunió a comunidades muy distintas que anteriormente habían tenido pocos motivos para relacionarse.

examples.en: The report tried to synthesise disparate findings into a single coherent set of recommendations.
examples.es: El informe intentaba sintetizar hallazgos muy dispares en un conjunto coherente de recomendaciones.

meaning_en: Not influenced by personal feelings; impartial and calm.
meaning_es: No influido por sentimientos personales; imparcial y sereno.
note: Not the same as cold or unfeeling; implies rational detachment prized in judges, scientists, and reviewers.

examples.en: A dispassionate reading of the evidence left little doubt about what had actually happened.
examples.es: Una lectura imparcial de las pruebas dejaba pocas dudas sobre lo que había ocurrido realmente.

examples.en: She tried to give a dispassionate account of the dispute, even though she was personally affected.
examples.es: Intentó dar una relación imparcial del conflicto, aunque estaba afectada personalmente.

meaning_en: Feeling doubt or uncertainty about something; not convinced.
meaning_es: Que siente dudas o incertidumbre sobre algo; que no está convencido.
collocation: dubious about the plan, remain dubious
note: Predicative when describing a person's uncertain state of mind ('was dubious about'); 'dubious' modifying a noun is a separate sense.

examples.en: She was dubious about the timeline from the start, and her scepticism proved well-founded.
examples.es: Desde el principio mostró escepticismo ante el calendario previsto, y sus dudas resultaron estar bien fundadas.

examples.en: He remained dubious even after the team presented three rounds of supporting data.
examples.es: Siguió sin estar convencido incluso después de que el equipo presentara tres rondas de datos de apoyo.

meaning_en: Deceitful, especially by saying one thing and doing another.
meaning_es: Engañoso, especialmente al decir una cosa y hacer otra.
note: The noun is 'duplicity'; the word focuses on deliberate two-facedness, not mere deception.

examples.en: His duplicitous dealings eventually alienated every business partner he had ever cultivated.
examples.es: Sus tratos engañosos acabaron alejando a todos los socios comerciales que había cultivado a lo largo del tiempo.

examples.en: She accused the agency of being duplicitous in its public statements about the accident.
examples.es: Acusó a la agencia de ser engañosa en sus declaraciones públicas sobre el accidente.
